paragraphs: Rusty Pelican has restaurants on Key Biscayne in Miami and in Tampa. Both take reservations and host private events, and holidays like Mother's Day and Thanksgiving bring in a lot of bookings.
Our job was to bring in those bookings through Google Ads and show what every ad dollar brought back in each city.

items.title: Reach people who are already looking
items.bodyHtml: We ran Google search ads aimed at people already searching for a place to eat, and tracked each click through to the booking.

items.title: Separate the campaigns by goal
items.bodyHtml: We ran separate campaigns for reservations, private events and seasonal dates. In Tampa, private events were the focus.

items.title: Plan around the big dates
items.bodyHtml: We ran seasonal campaigns ahead of days like Mother's Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas, when people book ahead.

items.title: Track every booking
items.bodyHtml: We set up conversion tracking on calls, reservations and form fills, and each month we report the results against what was spent.

items.title: Build the website
items.bodyHtml: We also designed and built the Rusty Pelican website. It has full-width photos, a menu split into sections, the chef's story and built-in reservations. There's more on our restaurant website design page.

results.explainHtml: How to read these numbers: a conversion is one tracked action, like a reservation, a call or a private-event inquiry. ROAS (return on ad spend) compares the tracked value of those conversions with what the ads cost.

accounts.name: Rusty Pelican Miami
accounts.standout: Mother's Day brought 155 conversions at $3.06 each. Thanksgiving brought 252 at $3.70 each.

accounts.name: Rusty Pelican Tampa
accounts.standout: Christmas and Thanksgiving were the top performers.
